item.title: A Bit of Freedom Goes a Long Way: Classical and Quantum Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning under a Generative Model
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Andris Ambainis, Joao F. Doriguello, Debbie Lim
We propose novel classical and quantum online algorithms for learning finite- and infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Our algorithms are based on a hybrid online-offline reinforcement learning model wherein the agent can, from time to time, freely interact with the environment in a generative sampling fashion, i.e., by having access to a ''simulator''. By employing known classical and new quantum algorithms for approximating optimal policies under a generative model within our learning algorithms, we show that it is possible to avoid several paradigms from RL like ''optimism in the face of uncertainty'' and ''posterior sampling'' and instead compute and use optimal policies directly, which yields better regret bounds compared to previous works. item.title: Physics-informed distribution of relaxation times estimation and latent-space condition monitoring of solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cells from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Žan Gorenc, Žiga Gradišar, Felix Mütter, Vanja Subotić, Pavle Boškoski
arXiv:2608.13305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating the distribution of relaxation times (DRT) fromelectrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is an ill-posed inverse problem that is highly sensitive to regularisation choices. We propose a physics-informed convolutional autoencoder that estimates DRT directly from EIS data without spectrum-specific tuning. A discretised relation between impedance and the DRT is embedded in the training process, constraining the network to produce impedance-consistent distributions. The model resolves overlapping relaxation processes in synthetic two-ZARC spectra and accurately reconstructs measurements from three independent solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cell datasets, with range-normalised errors below 1.1%. item.title: AutoQuREO: A Framework for Automated Quantum Resource Estimation and Optimization
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Harshkumar Oza, Aritra Sarkar, Syed Naqi Abbas, Rahul Bhowmick, Aryan Prakash, Prateek P Kulkarni, Krishna Kumar Sabapathy
arXiv:2608.12936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As quantum computing progresses from proof-of-principle demonstrations toward practical utility, a significant impediment is the need to augment algorithmic feasibility with system-level optimization across heterogeneous hardware and software stacks. item.title: 电磁—机械耦合问题的统一时空有限元求解框架
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Wei Gu, Li Zhu, Yansong Guo, Shizhong Liang, Feng Wu, Xindi Wei
该研究针对电磁—机械耦合瞬态问题，提出统一的时空有限元离散变分框架，以避免传统空间半离散加时间积分方法可能带来的数值耗散、能量漂移和辛结构破坏。作者构建时空有限元网格，并基于离散变分形式给出适用于无耗散与耗散系统的统一一步递推格式。通过纯电磁场、弹性动力学和顺序耦合电磁—机械问题等算例，展示了该方法在统一框架内求解位移场和电磁场的能力。

item.title: 受光子系统启发的束缚引力波
item.description:
📚 Physics News
该文以科普形式讨论一种受光子体系类比启发的“束缚”引力波概念。文章从通常意义上可传播的波动出发，说明引力波是时空结构中的扰动，并引出与光子系统中局域或束缚波态相联系的新观点。具体物理机制和理论细节需查阅原文。

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Variational Quantum Feature Learning for Reliable High-Dimensional Classification
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Syed Basha Shaik, Srihari Varma Mantena, Shaik Janbhasha, V. Malsoru, Ravikiran Reddy Kandadi, RADHAKRISHNAN S 等7位作者
High-dimensional classification remains challenging for hybrid quantum–classical learning because conventional variational quantum feature learning methods often assign equal importance to all input features and do not explicitly account for feature uncertainty. This paper presents Uncertainty-Aware Variational Quantum Feature Learning (UVQFL), a hybrid framework that combines adaptive feature weighting, uncertainty estimation, and variational quantum representation learning for reliable classification. The proposed framework incorporates an Adaptive Feature Confidence Module (AFCM) to estimate the contribution of individual input features before quantum encoding and an Uncertainty Estimation Module (UEM) to characterize feature reliability during the learning process. item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Congchao Wang, Diwakar Singh, Qiaozi Gao, Spyros Matsoukas, Yang Liu, Mahdi Namazifar
arXiv:2608.12585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Improving reasoning LLMs requires the ability to judge the quality of long reasoning traces for effective reasoning data curation, strong training signals during reinforcement learning, and an in-depth understanding of reasoning behaviors during model performance evaluation. Additionally, surfacing reasoning mistakes that the model makes would enable improving the model's performance at runtime through providing feedback. Due to the difficulty of this complex task on long reasoning traces, single-model judges (even frontier models) do not do well at identifying reasoning defects. item.title: 气候极端事件下华北平原玉米产量预测：作物模型—机器学习混合方法
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Haonan Tan, Dengpan Xiao, Huizi Bai, Yang Lu, Lihua Lv, Peipei Pan 等13位作者
该研究构建了将过程作物模型 APSIM 与随机森林、LightGBM 等机器学习模型结合的混合模拟框架，用于改进极端气候条件下华北平原春玉米和夏玉米产量预测。作者采用逐步回归和遗传算法筛选不同生育期的关键信息性极端气候指标，并将其与 APSIM 输出共同输入机器学习模型。结果显示，APSIM+RF+GA 表现最佳，可解释春玉米和夏玉米观测产量变异的 94% 和 93%，相较单独 APSIM 分别提高约 30% 和 31% 的模拟精度。

item.title: 规则还是塑形？面向 AI 安全设计的标度律研究
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Satoshi Takahashi, Nobuji Kouno, Masaaki Komatsu, Ryuji Hamamoto
该文研究 AI 安全系统中两类机制的权衡：训练时的“性格塑形”（如 RLHF、Constitutional AI）与推理时的规则执行（如过滤器和安全分类器）。作者建立了一个比较静态模型，用资源分配参数描述两者比例，并纳入规模增长导致的过滤退化、共模失效和性格脆弱性等因素。结果表明，最优策略通常位于内部解或偏向规则端，且随着部署规模扩大，仅会弱向性格塑形方向移动。

item.title: Achieving Near 21% Efficiency Organic Solar Cells through Controlled Packing of Fused-Ring Electron Acceptors
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Nan Wei, Tong Sun, Hao Lu, Xiaodong Wang, Xueqing Ma, Jiahe Zhang 等15位作者
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76532-1 Non radiative energy loss remains a challenge in non-fullerene organic solar cells. Wei et al. introduce chlorobenzene-functionalized acceptors that exhibit enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield with a distinct molecular packing mode, enabling a power conversion efficiency of 20.92%.
